title: Quick Sampler Tricks
intro: Quick Sampler turns any sound into a playable instrument in about three seconds. It is the fastest route from “that noise is interesting” to “that noise is now a bassline”.

tips.t: Know the four modes and pick deliberately
tips.d: Classic for straight playback, One Shot for drums and stabs, Slice to chop a loop across the keyboard, Recorder to sample live input. Choosing the mode is 90% of the work.

tips.t: Use Slice mode with Transient detection on any break
tips.d: Load a drum loop, switch to Slice, and every hit is mapped to its own key. Drag from the lower waveform display into the Tracks area to get the MIDI — the original groove, fully rearrangeable.

tips.t: Drag audio directly from the Tracks area into a loaded Quick Sampler
tips.d: Drag a region straight from the Tracks area into Quick Sampler's waveform display to swap the sound without leaving the plug-in. Drop it on the Original half to keep the file's own tuning, loudness, looping and length; drop it on Optimized and Quick Sampler analyses the file, optimises tuning, loudness and length, and adds loop and crossfade markers for you. Dropping a region triggers an offline bounce before it lands in the display, so give it a moment. (Dragging to the track header instead brings up a Replace Existing Sound dialog.) Glance over your filter and envelope after the swap rather than assuming everything carried across.

tips.t: Use Flex/Follow Tempo to lock a loop to the project
tips.d: Flex and Follow Tempo are two separate buttons, at the lower right of Quick Sampler's waveform display in Classic, One Shot and Slice modes. Turning Flex on by itself only plays the sample at its original speed for all note pitches — it does not chase the project tempo. Turn Flex on, then turn Follow Tempo on as well: with both active, slices stretch or contract according to the original tempo of the loop and the current project tempo, so the loop tracks tempo changes without shifting pitch.

tips.t: Set the root key correctly or nothing will be in tune
tips.d: Quick Sampler guesses the pitch. If your bass is a semitone out across the keyboard, this is why. Set it manually in the Pitch section.

tips.t: Drag MIDI out of Slice mode into the Tracks area
tips.d: The generated MIDI plays the slices in the original order. Now shuffle the notes and the break rearranges itself.

tips.t: Convert Quick Sampler to Sampler for full control
tips.d: Swap the instrument slot from Quick Sampler to Sampler and your loaded content transfers across automatically. Do it when you need multiple velocity layers, round robins or key zones. It is a one-way trip — Sampler settings will not open back up in Quick Sampler.
